subject: Dataset bridging: escrow, dry-run window, and giveback schedule
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@brightmart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dataset bridging: escrow, dry-run window, and giveback schedule

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short mutual action plan (MAP) focused on dataset exchange logistics and the acceptance window so your legal and procurement teams can review. High level:

- We provide an ephemeral evaluation bundle (prompt pack + ~5k redacted testcases) under an MPA with explicit non-production and no-redistribution constraints.
- BrightMart runs a 5-business-day acceptance dry-run in your staging environment.
- A 7-day giveback/takedown window follows acceptance for any retention/cleanup steps.
- We place a checksum/fingerprint in escrow so both sides can validate provenance; Redwood retains a sealed copy with doc timestamps.

I attached a draft MAP (MAP-BrightMart-v1.2.pdf) and the prompt pack stub (brightmart_promptpack_v2.zip). The prompt pack is zipped and contains sample inputs, expected labels, and an acceptance runner script (readme included).

Next steps I propose:
1) Please share any required redlines to the MPA by EOD Wed, Nov 3.
2) If procurement needs a separate SOW/PO, loop procurement@brightmart.com and we’ll route a DocuSign envelope.
3) We’ll provision ephemeral credentials for your staging cluster the morning after sign-off (we suggest Nov 8 start).

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Technical: end-to-end run of the provided runner across your subset (>=95% of tests execute without data leakage triggers).
- Security: no downstream copying; access audited via token ID and IP allowlist.
- Operational: dry-run latency and throughput baselines recorded in Redwood Console.

Quick ask: can Tom or your procurement lead confirm whether BrightMart needs an escrow agent on record or a simple sealed checksum is sufficient?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-BrightMart-v1.2.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]
[Attachment: brightmart_promptpack_v2.zip (ZIP, 12MB)]
From: Claire Huang <claire@brightmart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightmart.com>, procurement@brightmart.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dataset bridging: escrow, dry-run window, and giveback schedule

Logan —

Thanks for the clear plan and the docs. Quick replies from our side:

- Procurement flagged the MPA section on custody. They want a hard escrow agent listed in the agreement (we can provide a short list of preferred firms) rather than only a sealed checksum.
- Security asked for an explicit 90-day auto-delete clause after the giveback window unless a separate retention waiver is signed.
- We will only run the provided prompt pack in a non-prod VPC with outbound disabled; please confirm Redwood’s runner script works offline (no outbound calls).

I’m stamping Nov 3 as our internal target for redlines, but procurement may push to Nov 5 depending on legal bandwidth. Tom — can you confirm preferred escrow vendors and whether procurement will need a PO ahead of DocuSign?

Also: we’ll need a short technical dry-run checklist showing exactly how the runner asserts no-exfiltration so our security team can sign off (hash checks, token revocation steps, and IP allowlist verification).

Claire Huang
Sr. Product Manager, BrightMart

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@brightmart.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightmart.com>, procurement@brightmart.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dataset bridging: escrow, dry-run window, and giveback schedule

Claire / Tom / procurement —

Appreciate the feedback. Quick answers and an updated deliverable set attached:

1) Escrow agent: we can accept a named third-party escrow firm or hold a sealed checksum in a neutral S3 bucket with time-stamped logs; both are fine for us. If you provide vendor names, we’ll add the agent block to the MPA.

2) Auto-delete: Redwood is comfortable with a 90-day auto-delete post-giveback. We’ll add a clause to the MPA that requires a signed retention waiver to extend beyond that.

3) Offline runner: confirmed — the included runner is self-contained and requires only local execution and checksum verification. No outbound telemetry or third-party calls. We will provide an explicit dry-run checklist and a short script to revoke tokens on completion.

I attached an updated MAP (v1.2) with the escrow agent placeholder and the dataset fingerprint (dataset-fingerprint-20261101.txt). Also attached a short dry-run checklist (bottom of MAP) that enumerates the hash verification and token revocation steps.

Proposed timeline (updated):
- Nov 5: BrightMart redlines due (if possible); Nov 8 fallback if procurement needs extra time.
- Nov 9: MPA sign & DocuSign routing.
- Nov 10–16: 5-business-day dry-run (Nov 10, 11, 12, 13, 16).
- Nov 17–23: 7-day giveback and tidy-up (content removal, audit export).

Action items:
- Tom / procurement: confirm escrow vendor OR ack sealed-checksum approach by Nov 5.
- BrightMart Security: review dry-run checklist; request edits before Nov 9.

— Logan
[Attachment: MAP-BrightMart-v1.2.pdf (updated, PDF, 200KB)]
[Attachment: dataset-fingerprint-20261101.txt (TXT, 1KB)]
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightmart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Claire Huang <claire@brightmart.com>
Cc: procurement@brightmart.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dataset bridging: escrow, dry-run window, and giveback schedule

Logan / Claire —

Procurement and legal reviewed the MAP. We’re good with the sealed-checksum approach so long as Redwood can provide immutable time-stamped logs and an S3-stored sealed copy (read-only to BrightMart until a dispute). That saves us time vs. third-party escrow onboarding.

Two quick asks before we sign:
1) Please add a clause that Redwood will provide an "audit export" (log bundle of token IDs, IP allowlist checks, and the run output hashes) within 48 hours of our request during the giveback window.
2) Confirm the runner will produce per-testcase hashes so our security team can run independent verification.

If you can add those two items to the MAP and route the DocuSign, procurement will sign and we can start provisioning Nov 10 as proposed.

Tom Ellis
Director, Strategic Procurement — BrightMart
[Attachment: none]
